name: Biroot Locking Is a Static Terminal-Pair Certificate
statement: For nested ample $A\subsetneq B$, call the pair lower-root-locked when, for every $x\in B\setminus A$, the root remains connected to $x$ after deleting from $\widehat G(B,A)$ every edge labelled by a coordinate in $L_A(x)$. This finite ordering-free condition certifies that $(\Delta_B,\Delta_A)$ is not relatively shellable. Define upper-root-locking by applying the same condition to the complementary pair $Q_F\setminus B\subsetneq Q_F\setminus A$. It is equivalent to $B\setminus\{x\}$ being nonample for every $x\in B\setminus A$. Therefore a pair locked at both roots admits neither a first nor a last relative shelling facet, and both failures are decided by labelled cut tests in the two rooted graphs.
proof: The rooted cut criterion says that lower-root-locking excludes every ample one-concept extension of $A$ within $B$. A relative shelling would have to begin with such an extension, so none exists. For the upper condition, $B\setminus\{x\}$ is ample exactly when $(Q_F\setminus B)\cup\{x\}$ is ample. Applying the same rooted cut criterion to the complementary nested pair proves the deletion characterization and excludes a final relative shelling facet.
comments: Root locking supplies a direct nonshellability certificate without storing a shelling or carrier order. Biroot locking is necessary for relative terminality; this result does not by itself classify all locked presentations.
